prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of a living room with a recessed ceiling and hanging chandelier above, a couch against the back-left window wall (~3.5–4.5 m away), a TV and stand on the right (~3–4 m away), a large framed portrait board on the left (~0.5–2 m away), and a standing woman in the center. Across the five frames, the woman's silhouette brightens and expands as she approaches from roughly 3 m away in front of the couch in frame 1 to about 0.8–1 m directly in front of the camera wearer (within arm's reach) by frame 5, while the framed board on the lower left becomes intensely white in frame 5 at roughly 0.5 m (also within arm's reach of both the wearer and the woman) alongside a small held booklet between them. The map clearly shows the woman's forward approach, her depth separation when occluding the couch behind her, and the sharp tilt of the foreground board in frame 5, even where bright window backlighting in RGB washes out the background. However, the monocular depth estimation is unreliable on the ceiling and upper corners—which appear artificially bright as if closer than 1 m—and flattens the recessed wall behind the chandelier into a dark void while losing fine depth contours of the woman's face and hands.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates key foreground and mid-ground instances across the room, tracking the approaching woman (from ~3 m in frame 1 to ~0.8–1 m in frame 5, about 1–2.5 m ahead of the couch and TV) and the TV on the right (~3–4 m away in frames 2–5), while illustrating how the woman progressively occludes the couch directly behind her and becomes cropped below the chest/shoulders in frames 3–5. It highlights the spatial footprints and occlusions of the woman, couch, and TV screen against a black background, separating the overlapping couch segments on either side of the woman in frame 2. However, the map is heavily unreliable in its semantic labels and temporal consistency: in frame 1 it falsely segments the three painted figures inside the flat family portrait on the left (~1.5–2 m away) as real 'person' instances and labels the couch as 'bed'/'bench', while in frame 2 it mislabels the entire portrait board (~1.5 m away) as a 'tv'. Furthermore, it misclassifies part of the overhead chandelier (~2.5 m high) as a 'traffic light' in frames 1 and 5, labels the couch as a 'chair' in frames 3–4, mistakes the woman's head (~1 m away, cropped at the bottom of frame 4) for a 'dog', and mislabels the handheld booklet within arm's reach (~0.6 m) at the bottom left of frame 5 as a 'laptop'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body skeletons on a black background, detecting only the standing woman in frames 1 and 3 while completely missing her in frames 2, 4, and 5 as well as any hands (no magenta skeletons appear in any frame). In frame 1, the full upper-body skeleton (~3 m away in front of the couch) shows her torso facing mostly toward the camera wearer with her head tilted slightly right, her left arm bent at the elbow bringing her wrist across her waist within reach of the object she holds, and her right arm hanging down; her legs below the hips are omitted. In frame 3, as she steps closer (~1.8 m away) and her lower torso drops out of the bottom of the frame, only a partial skeleton of her head, shoulders, right upper arm, and a single torso line is detected, showing her still oriented toward the camera wearer. While the skeleton in frame 1 makes the bend of her left elbow and shoulder alignment easier to read than against her dark clothing in the RGB image, the map is highly unreliable due to total detection failures in three of the five frames, missing hand keypoints when she holds the booklet within arm's reach, and false-negative omissions as her body is progressively cropped at the bottom edge.
